{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZZE9NQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDAaUk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 35, "title": "Correct V9938 SCREEN 7/8 VRAM interleaving across ports, rendering and commands", "body": "## Problem

V9938 SCREEN 7/8 use mode-dependent VRAM addressing. Current `vdp.rs` CPU reads/writes, bitmap access and sprite fetches use flat indices; `vdp_command.rs` also directly accesses flat byte addresses. Consequently, data written in another mode is interpreted incorrectly after switching to SCREEN 7/8, and vice versa. Consistent flat addressing can conceal the error in same-mode tests.

This is a specification-based MSX2 compatibility defect affecting shared bitmap, sprite and command data. No commercial-title failure was observed during this investigation.

## Expected outcome

Keep one stable 128 KiB VRAM backing store, with correct logical-to-physical decoding for each supported mode and access path. Using physical storage order, SCREEN 7/8 map logical address `L` to `((L >> 1) | ((L & 1) << 16)) & 0x1ffff`; other supported modes retain their applicable linear decoding. Changing modes must reinterpret existing bytes without rearranging or clearing storage.

CPU ports, bitmap pixels, sprite tables, logical commands and byte commands must agree on the same stored data. Preserve existing MSX1 behavior and supported MSX2/BASIC functionality.

## Context

- Baseline: `8727ed507b04a862af2bc529074645702fa4dc31`; clean local HEAD matches GitHub main. The inspected open Issue/PR collection is empty. Initial MSX2 work [#11 / PR #12](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/12) supplied these paths; this task corrects their addressing.
- Relevant code: `crates/msx-core/src/vdp.rs` (`control`, `read`, `write`, `advance`, bitmap helpers and sprites), `vdp_command.rs`, direct VRAM consumers in `basic.rs`, and original fixtures in `firmware.rs`. Existing regression coverage includes `crates/msx-core/tests/msx2.rs` and `tests/msx2.spec.js`.
- [V9938 hardware measurements](https://openmsx.org/vdp-vram-timing/vdp-timing.html), under “Multi-bank page mode reads,” explain the address rotation and its observable effect on mode switches. The experiment concerns a Philips NMS8250 V9938.
- The [manufacturer manual](https://www.dinoboards.com.au/assets/video-v9958/yamaha_v9938.pdf), printed pages 2–3, 7, 46–53 and the command/sprite chapters, defines the port counter, GRAPHIC 6/7 (SCREEN 7/8), pages and tables. [Upstream CPU/sprite decoding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/master/src/video/VDP.cc) and [command address calculations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/master/src/video/VDPCmdEngine.cc) corroborate the mapping; use them as behavioral evidence, independently authoring code and fixtures.
- Existing PR #34 [CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/39958946734) report 130 Rust and 84 browser tests passing, including existing video tests. Several video assertions directly populate the flat layout, so these passes do not establish correct interleaving. No builds or tests were run for this planning task.
- Scope is address decoding and its integration. VRAM arbitration, command speed/color corrections, expansion VRAM and exact mid-command mode-change timing remain separate limitations. Commercial compatibility remains unestablished.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement consistent mode-dependent decoding across CPU read prefetch/read-ahead and writes, bitmap rendering and drawing, sprite attribute/color/pattern fetches, and all existing command memory paths. Keep the address counter logical; preserve documented R14 carry, mode-dependent wrapping, latches and absent expansion-memory behavior. Document the backing-store convention.
- [ ] Add independent native regressions that fail on the current implementation. Write distinct bytes through ports in a linear mode, switch without clearing VRAM, and inspect SCREEN 7/8 reads and pixels; test the reverse direction and SCREEN 7↔8 preservation. Include fixed expected pairs such as `00001h→10000h`, `00002h→00001h`, and `10000h→08000h`, rather than calculating every expectation with the production helper.
- [ ] Cover even/odd addresses, both 64 KiB physical banks, R14/16 KiB counter boundaries, full 128 KiB wrap, and buffered reads across boundaries and ordinary mode switches. Mode changes must preserve stored bytes; reset must retain its existing clearing behavior.
- [ ] Verify SCREEN 7 packed nibbles and SCREEN 8 direct-color pixels on both display pages, with scroll and existing alternate-page/interlace coverage retained. Upload sprite attribute, color and pattern data through ports, including cross-mode interpretation, and assert visible pixels plus representative collision/overflow behavior. Preserve existing table-base masks and sprite color rules.
- [ ] Exercise logical pixel/fill/copy/readback and byte fill/copy/CPU-transfer command paths in both modes, including bank alternation, page boundaries and overlapping/reverse copies. Check results through ports or another mode as well as pixels, retaining CE/TR, STOP, logical-operation and absent-expansion regressions. Update flat-layout fixtures without weakening coverage.
- [ ] Add or extend an original Z80 browser fixture that exposes cross-mode interpretation through real ports and verifies Canvas pixels at both `/` and `/msx-rust/`. Retain existing diagnostic, C-BIOS, SCREEN 5–8 BASIC drawing, input/audio and reset coverage. Audit direct BASIC VRAM access, including `VPOKE`, for coherent addressing while preserving documented bounds and supported semantics; do not expand the language.
- [ ] Preserve MSX1/MSX2 firmware/slot behavior, PSG/SCC audio, disk, SRAM persistence, Wasm/browser lifecycle and ownership/provenance safeguards. Any distributed fixture must be independently authored with documented licensing; no proprietary ROM acquisition or human gameplay is required.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs and reports the README checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, using documented dependency setup as needed. Update affected documentation and complete source-Issue/full-diff review under `docs/review-guidelines.md`; resolve blocking findings before merge and distinguish passed, failed and unperformed validation.

## Optional validation

Compare the same independently authored cross-mode probe with openMSX or an available hardware recording. Record exact configuration and observations if performed. This comparison was not run and is not a merge prerequisite.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
